$comment: Mutation arms cutting the types of package anyparse.format. Format and rules: docs/testing.md, Declared arms.

arms.name: M-FIRST-LINE-FIT
arms.note: expression-position FitLine goes back to placing a body by its FIRST line: a body that cannot render flat takes the plain glue, whose width gate measures only that line, so it glues to the head line again

arms.name: M-STRICT-HEAD-DELIM-OFF
arms.note: restores the blanket refusal, so an expression-`for` whose body is a keyword-led construct opening a delimiter leaves the head line again

arms.name: M-WRAP-SEPAFTER-ALWAYS
arms.note: a synthesized block records a source `;` after its statement, so the block writer appends one after the `}` of an `if` it braced

arms.name: M-SSB-CHAIN-TRAILSEMI-OFF
arms.note: the if/else chain scan ignores the `;` kept after the terminal else body, so brace removal strips the chain and writes `else b();;`

arms.name: M-TRY-TRAILSEMI-GATE-OFF
arms.note: a `try` group de-braces although its last catch body carries a kept `;`, so the writer emits `catch (e) b();;`

arms.name: M-SSB-TAIL-SEALED-NONE
arms.note: no ctor reads as sealing its own tail, so a block, switch or do-while at the end of a body stops shielding the trailing `else` and the branch keeps braces it does not need

arms.name: M-SSB-OPEN-TRAIL-NONE
arms.note: a body whose single statement carries an OPEN trailing comment reads as carrying none, so the comment stops travelling with the statement the de-brace lifts out

arms.name: M-SSB-DANGLING-NONE
arms.note: no statement tail reads as a dangling `if`, so the de-brace stops refusing a body whose last statement would capture the enclosing `else`

arms.name: M-EICR-BOUNDARY-SKIP
arms.find: case WrapBoundary(inner): afterCond ? rewrap(scan(inner, trailing, true), d -> Doc.WrapBoundary(d)) : Scanning(true);
arms.note: a `WrapBoundary` past the condition is skipped whole instead of scanned, so the body's own boundary hides the anchor and every else-if comment reflow refuses

arms.name: M-EICR-HEADTEXT-ANY
arms.note: every rendered token reads as head text, so a `//`, a `}` or a `;` no longer ends the head line and the comment anchors past the position it belongs to

arms.name: M-EICR-SOFTLINE-ANCHOR
arms.note: a width-only break anchors the comment as readily as an unconditional one, so a body that merely COULD break takes the trailing comment the reflow was written to refuse

arms.name: M-SSB-DOBODY-KEEP
arms.note: the do-body arm stops substituting its single clean statement for the block, so `do { g(); } while (c)` keeps braces the suppress frame is explicitly told not to gate

arms.name: M-LOOPIF-NEVER
arms.note: the loop-body probe never sees an `if` with an `else`, so `loopBodyIfElseNext` never breaks the body under the header and every glued shape stays glued

arms.name: M-LOOPIF-ALWAYS
arms.note: the same probe answers yes for every body, so a bare guard `if` and a non-`if` body break under the loop header alongside the shape the knob exists for

arms.name: M-LOOPIF-NOWRAP
arms.note: the one-level unwrap answers no, so a `do ... while` body - an `HxDoWhileBody.ExprBody` around the `if` - is invisible to the probe while the bare `for` / `while` body still reaches it

arms.name: M-SSB-TRY-SUBST-OFF
arms.note: the try/catch group verdict is computed and then not applied - neither the wrap direction nor the de-brace one reaches a body

arms.name: M-SSB-TRY-DEBRACE-NONE
arms.note: verdict 2 can no longer strip a braced try/catch body, so only the wrap direction of the group verdict survives

arms.name: M-SSB-BARE-ILLEGAL
arms.note: an ALREADY bare body blocks the group verdict instead of passing it, so a try/catch that is half de-braced is wrapped back up rather than finished

arms.name: M-SSB-VALUE-WRAP-OFF
arms.note: the value-if/value-try symmetry wrap never fires, so a bare branch opposite a braced one keeps its shape and the semicolon drop that rides on the wrap stops happening

arms.name: M-SSB-CHAIN-TAIL-OFF
arms.find: return elseBody != null && keepsBraces(elseBody, drop, symmetry, suppress, false, stmt.elseBodyTrailPresent == true, false);
arms.note: the chain scan stops probing the FINAL else branch, so an asymmetry that only the tail of an else-if chain carries no longer forces the earlier branches to keep their braces

arms.name: M-SSB-ELEM-TRAIL-COMMENT-NONE
arms.note: the de-braced statements OWN same-line trailing comment is never read, so only a block openTrailing comment can travel and the else-body splice loses its comment

arms.name: M-SSB-SYMMETRY-ONLY-BLIND
arms.note: under symmetry-only (`singleStatementBraces: symmetric`) no body reads as brace-keeping, so the repair direction never sees a braced sibling to mirror

arms.name: M-CHAIN-STAIRCASE-OFF
arms.find: if (chainBodyInner(second) == null) return chainHeadGate(cols, body, second, sameLine, lineWidth);
arms.replace:
if (chainBodyInner(second) == null) return chainHeadGate(cols, body, second, sameLine, lineWidth);
	return sameLine;
arms.note: a chain of three links or more never staircases, so an over-long chain keeps the same-line layout instead of breaking every link

arms.name: M-CHAIN-HEAD-GATE-OFF
arms.note: a two-link chain whose link hides its head in a construct group glues on the keyword alone again, so an over-wide head wraps its condition instead of moving the link to the next line

arms.name: M-SLOT-PROBE-BREAK-NONE
arms.find: return indent >= 0 && indent == slotIndent(fl, false) ? brk : null;
arms.note: a body slot wrapped in a chain gate's probe no longer reads as droppable, so a cuddled comprehension over a gated chain opens its bracket on a line of its own

arms.name: M-PAREN-PIN-NONE
arms.note: no glued body carries a pinnable collapse probe, so the arrow-continuation rescue has nothing to pin and the body breaks instead of gluing

arms.name: M-GLUE-NEVER-BREAKS
arms.find: return lineWidth <= 0 ? glued : Doc.IfGluedFirstLineExceeds(lineWidth, cols, breakLayout(cols, body), glued);
arms.note: the glued body is emitted with no width test at all, so a header whose glued first line overflows never falls back to the break layout

arms.name: M-CASE-CTRLFLOW-GLUE-NOT-REFUSED
arms.note: a control-flow body that cannot render flat glues to its label again, so its continuation lines render at the head's indent and read as if the statement had left the branch

arms.name: M-SSB-CHAIN-THEN-TRAILSEMI-OFF
arms.note: the if/else chain scan ignores a `;` kept after a then-body, so brace removal strips the rest of the chain while that body keeps its braces - an asymmetric chain

arms.name: M-SSB-ELSE-SPINE-STOP
arms.note: a trailing `if` that HAS its own `else` still reads as dangling, so the spine walk stops continuing into that else branch and the body keeps braces it does not need

arms.name: M-EICR-AFTERCOND-RESET
arms.note: the after-condition flag is not threaded from one sibling to the next, so a comment anchor that sits past the condition in a LATER item is never recognised

arms.name: M-SSB-GATE8-ANY-POSITION
arms.note: gate 8's keep stops being restricted to then-position, so an else body whose single statement is an `if` no longer collapses into an `else if`

arms.name: M-GAP-DOC-PRECEDENCE
arms.note: the after-doc blank beats `beforeDocCommentEmptyLines: none`, the reverse of the writer's precedence, so the check demands a blank between two doc-commented members the writer removes

arms.name: M-GAP-MULTILINE-AFTER-NOBLANK
arms.note: a forced zero beats the multi-line rule, though the writer tops the empty gap up afterwards, so the check demands a tight gap before a multi-line doc-commented member the writer sets off

arms.name: M-GAP-DOCLED-ANY-COMMENT
arms.note: every leading comment counts as a doc comment, in the writer and the check alike, so a line-comment-led field is set off by blanks it never had

arms.name: M-BREAK-COMMITTED-BARE
arms.note: a literal broken by its own width is laid out bare where the next write reads it in a `BodyGroup` every width probe defers, so a method chain dot-breaks and an arrow body leaves `->` on the first write and both glue back on the second

arms.name: M-ALLMAN-GLUED-SPACE-KEPT
arms.find: case Doc.Concat([Doc.OptSpace(' '), body]) if (BreakCommits.decisionMapped(body, (brk, _) -> brk) != null):
arms.note: the layout a list is offered for an Allman body break keeps the glued placement's space, so a cuddled head measured on it counts a column the output never has and opens at exactly the limit

arms.name: M-ALLMAN-GLUED-SPACE-UNGUARDED
arms.find: case Doc.Concat([Doc.OptSpace(' '), body]) if (BreakCommits.decisionMapped(body, (brk, _) -> brk) != null):
arms.note: the space is dropped also before a body that only ends in the decision (a nested `for`), gluing `)for` in the offered layout

arms.name: M-WIDTH-RULE-TAIL-UNREAD
arms.find: Doc.Group(Doc.IfWidthExceeds(_, Doc.LeadingBreak(cols, brk, token), _)) if (token != null):
arms.replace: Doc.Group(Doc.IfLineExceeds(_, Doc.LeadingBreak(cols, brk, token), _)) if (token != null):
arms.note: the Allman break of a lineLength-rule literal is not offered to its one-item list, which stays laddered where the next write cuddles

arms.name: M-BODY-EDGE-STATED-IGNORED
arms.note: a stated type-body edge count stops winning, so `<kind>EmptyLines.beginType: 0` leaves the source blank `afterLeftCurly: keep` carries

arms.name: M-SSB-WRAP-FROM-NONE
arms.note: no body reads as one the symmetry wrap braced, so the own-line comment before a bare branch stays outside the braces the repair adds, dedented onto the head with the brace alone below it

arms.name: M-SSB-THEN-SKIP
arms.note: the else-position skip list also exempts a then-position `switch`, so `if (a) switch k {…} else { … }` stays half-braced under symmetric

arms.name: M-SSB-WRAP-FROM-UNLIFTED
arms.find: return node == raw || Reflect.isEnumValue(node) && paramAt(cast node, 0) == raw;
arms.note: a value branch lifted into a statement inside its new block no longer reads as wrapped, so its head-gap comments stay outside the braces

arms.name: M-CLAUSE-GAP-NO-ADOPT
arms.note: a catch body the try group braces leaves the clause's comments outside the new braces, with the `{` alone below them

arms.name: M-WSP-ADD-NOOP
arms.note: adding a side leaves the policy as it was, so `macro : T` loses its pinned space before the colon and writes `macro: T` / `macro:T`

arms.name: M-SIBLING-DECIDE-OFF
arms.note: no list decides: every slot stays unresolved, each sibling renders its own form, so a switch keeps the mix under anyBreak

arms.name: M-SIBLING-OFFER-UNALIASED
arms.note: the offer is never committed: a widest unit whose only over-wide part is a pivot literal leads the spread on this pass and not on the next, so the writer needs a second pass

arms.name: M-SIBLING-VOTE-ANY-NEGATIVE
arms.note: any negative width reads as a vote, so a number another rule wrote is overwritten by the verdict

arms.name: M-CASE-BODY-STANDS-ON-WRAPPED-LABEL
arms.note: a case body glues to the last row of a wrapped label whenever that row plus the body fits

arms.name: M-SIBLING-BODY-HELD-NOT-MEASURED
arms.find: final held: Null<Doc> = count == 1 ? last : null;
arms.note: a comment-held statement votes as a plain body and stops measuring its glued form

arms.name: M-SIBLING-BODY-SOLE-SHAPE-DOES-NOT-LEAD
arms.note: a sole statement its shape keeps below the label stops moving its siblings

arms.name: M-SIBLING-BODY-IGNORES-FITLINE
arms.note: a body below its head under a policy that never asks to stand beside it votes, so a next-line switch moves on a fitLine knob it does not use

arms.name: M-SIBLING-BODY-SLOT-NOT-INLINE
arms.note: the slot hook stops inlining, so every body below its head evaluates its facts, the glue predicate among them, even in a list that does not share

arms.name: M-DOC-SPLIT-LEAD-ANY-PREDECESSOR
arms.note: two adjacent doc comments read as a split lead, which withdraws the before-doc blank from a member that should have it

arms.name: M-DOC-GAP-SPLIT-LEAD-IGNORED
arms.note: member-order demands a before-doc blank above a split-led member that fmt never writes
